cells.tense: You are choosing the direction of what you grow right now, with the pen in your hand.
cells.act: hold your shape under the weight
cells.ask: Keep the direction of a growing thing you care about steady for seven days. When the pull comes to correct it or explain it, stay where you put it and don't grip harder.
cells.core:
You can look at something you're growing and decide what it's for without forcing it — this much light, this much time, and that's the call. The direction is clear and it isn't bent around keeping the week comfortable. The thing grows sturdier because someone is steering it, and the steering has a light hand on it.

Holding a shape costs something. A different outcome gets wanted, or the week wants a different pace, and you'll feel the pull to correct or to explain. Stay put anyway. Keep that direction for seven days, take the weight as it arrives, and don't tighten around it. What you're growing gets its spine from your staying, not from your force.
cells.sheetLine: You can decide what you're growing and stay with it.
cells.verb: pointing attention and energy at chosen ends, and meaning it
cells.place: where you tend what is growing

cells.tense: You will be bracing an outcome before it arrives, tightening your grip on something you cannot write in advance.
cells.act: notice what is true across every layer of it
cells.ask: Stay with a growing thing beyond the moment you'd normally step in. Notice what's already true of it — soil, light, pace — before changing anything at all.
cells.core:
You've got hold of the wheel and you're steering with both hands. The outcome is specific, and you're pulling the thing toward it — more water, better light, the faster fix — because waiting feels like losing. From the bed, the grip reads as force.

Knowing a thing has another face than steering it. Stay with what you're growing past the moment you'd normally step in, and notice what's already true of it across all of it — not what it needs, not what it could be, what it is right now. Then your hands can act from what's actually there. Same wheel, different grip, and the white knuckles have somewhere to rest.
cells.sheetLine: You're forcing an outcome that hasn't happened yet.
cells.verb: pointing attention and energy at chosen ends, and meaning it
cells.place: where you tend what is growing

cells.tense: You were standing at a door already behind you, and the steering got left there.
cells.act: do the thing in your own way, without proving it
cells.ask: Do something for a growing thing your own particular way. No explaining it afterward, no checking if it was right — do it your way and stop.
cells.core:
You tend what's growing, and direction isn't getting picked right now. Things get tended by habit, and the question of what any of it is for has stopped being asked. That isn't a flaw in you. It's a tired line sitting next to a door that closed some time back, and pushing harder won't refill it.

Trying isn't the way back. Doing something your own way is. Choose a small act for something you're growing and do it the way only you would — no explaining, no checking whether it was right, no proving. Not big and not correct, just unmistakably yours. Doing it your way puts charge back on the line, and picking a direction comes after.
cells.sheetLine: Start choosing again by doing something your way.
cells.verb: pointing attention and energy at chosen ends, and meaning it
cells.place: where you tend what is growing

cells.tense: You are steering what you grow and not noticing your hands are on the wheel.
cells.act: put your own name on what is already yours
cells.ask: Take one call you've made about something you're growing — light, pace, what stays — and set it down on paper in your own hand. Keep the page.
cells.core:
Calls keep getting made about what you're growing — this much light, this much time, this stays and this goes — and asking you, you'd say it just went that way. The choices are real and they're yours, and your name isn't on them. What's growing reads them differently.

Before the next move, sign what's already done. Take a call you've made about something you're tending and set it down on paper in your own hand — one line, kept where you can see it. That isn't a new direction and it isn't a new habit. It's the direction already running, finally acknowledged, and the acknowledging is the whole shift.
